title: Frederick II (ministerial rescript) to Louis Michell (London), Berlin 28 Dec 1751, KHA Prins Willem V inv. 198 (DECODE R1955), in Michell's envoy code

documents.shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, Prins Willem V inv. 198 (DECODE R1955)
documents.route: Berlin -> London (Dutch interceptors' copy, The Hague)

plaintext.source: Ministerial rescript; not in the Politische Correspondenz; no printed or online decipherment found.

transcription.source: DECODE images P2 (first page) and P1, one line per manuscript line
transcription.notes: NOTES give 295 distinct; the measured count is 296 (half-groups such as 1½ and uncertain readings marked ? count as written).

system.summary: Michell's envoy code of 1751-52: a large numerical code of groups 2-5346 with half-groups (1½, 150½, 660½) and homophones even for de and que.

diacritics.note: Half-groups (a fraction ½ written after the integer) are separate codes; some groups underlined once or twice, function not established.

system.sibling_key: Added by WAINUT (11 Oct 2026): the code of Michell's own reports to the King (DECODE R1050, 5 Sep 1752; R1051, 12 Nov 1751), whose contemporary Dutch decipherments give 271 code values (targets/michell1751/key1751/scripts/envoy_key.py). Not the cabinet code of R1957 (targets/michell1751/); DECODE R1953 (von der Hellen, 4 Jan 1752) is a different, smaller code.
system.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from michell1751 under the one-key rule. 296 distinct of 362 groups (measured on transcription_r1955.txt; WAINUT's R1955_tx.txt counts 360, keeping one nine-digit run as one group).

prior_solution.where: Ministerial rescript, not in the Politische Correspondenz; no printed or online decipherment found

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the images. WAINUT contribution (11-12 Oct 2026): the images and the DECODE transcriptions of R1050/R1051 were fetched with a WAINUT DECODE account; the analysis was automated (see NOTES); human interventions on this target beyond setting the goal are not recorded.
tools: key1751/scripts in targets/michell1751/: envoy_key.py, decode.py, coherence.py, circular.py, compare_tx.py

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R1955 (and R1957, targets/michell1751/) images with the cookie.
R1955 (the other letter of the same date, ministerial rescript) transcribed in full: 362 groups.
R1955 vs R1957: 19 shared distinct groups, chance collisions; 296 distinct in 362, commonest group 5 times: large homophonic code with nothing for ciphertext-only analysis.
Printed or online decipherment of R1955 sought; the ministerial rescripts are not in the Politische Correspondenz; none found.
DECODE R1953 (von der Hellen to the King, 4 Jan 1752) checked as a sibling of R1955: different, smaller code.
WAINUT: R1955 transcribed independently from the DECODE images (360 groups; one unsplit nine-digit run) (R1955_tx.txt).
WAINUT: R1955 against the cabinet keys: v1 gives a value to 10 of 360 groups (2.8%), v2 to 20 (5.6%), against 181 of 548 (33.0%) and 381 (69.5%) for R1957: R1955 is not in the cabinet code.

WAINUT: table of Michell's envoy code (271 codes, 512 pairs) built from DECODE's transcriptions of the contemporary Dutch decipherments of Michell's reports R1050 and R1051 (key1751/scripts/envoy_key.py; table not committed); applied to R1955: 95 of 360 groups (26.4%) decoded; adjacent decoded words attested as French word pairs 19 of 30 against 11.1 for permutations (p = 0.001; with PC 8-9 only as corpus 14 vs 9.5, p = 0.046; the right v1 decode of R1957 scores only p = 0.28 on this test).

WAINUT circular-letter test, rule fixed in advance: LCS of R1955's 77 decoded words with each French PC 8-9 letter, z against 100 shuffles; best candidate (22 Dec 1751 - 10 Jan 1752) PC 5268 z = 2.69, highest control PC 5117 z = 4.85; no candidate qualifies; positive control finds a 17% word sample in its source at z 27.6-31.3 and in a 50% paraphrase at 5.8-10.9 (key1751/scripts/circular.py).

WAINUT prior-art check: this folder's predecessor (michell1751, Bourdeau, 19 Sep 2026) had transcribed R1955. A contemporary Dutch decipherment of R1955 may exist in Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 159 (not digitised); not consulted.
WAINUT transcriptions compared with Bourdeau's (compare_tx.py): R1955 352 of 360 groups agree, 8 differences.

Split from michell1751 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1955 is in Michell's envoy code, not the cabinet code of R1957, so it is its own entry. Fraction re-counted from R1955_reading_line.txt: 95 of 360 groups have a value.

validation.notes: Whole-word code decoded in isolated fragments (95 of 360 groups, mostly single words between unread groups); the letter n-gram test has no continuous text to score. WAINUT's word-pair coherence test (19 of 30 adjacent pairs attested against 11.1 for permutations, p = 0.001) is the statistical check.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The contemporary Dutch decipherments of Michell's own reports R1050/R1051 (271 code values, from DECODE's transcriptions) were matched to R1955 by WAINUT: 95 of 360 groups (26.4%) take a value, against 2.8-5.6% for the cabinet code, and adjacent decoded words are coherent above chance (19/30 against 11.1, p = 0.001); fragments only.
outcome.fraction_read_source: R1955_reading_line.txt: 95 of 360 groups with a value from the envoy table (WAINUT's group division of R1955_tx.txt), '·' counted as unread

gaps.item: R1955, 265 of 360 groups without a value in the envoy table
gaps.detail: The table comes from two decipherments of Michell's reports (R1050, R1051); further decipherments (probably KHA A31-1181) are not online, and a contemporary decipherment of R1955 may be in Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 159, not digitised. Not in print: ministerial rescripts are not in the Politische Correspondenz.

outcome.notes: WAINUT's result (PR #29), checked here: transcription compared and fraction re-counted. The subject cannot be stated beyond Dutch affairs (the Prince Stadholder, the States) and a negotiation involving Vienna. Split 14 Oct 2026 from michell1751.
